stem: Before a client receives deep sedation in a procedure room, the nurse discovers that the emergency airway equipment normally kept in the room has been removed for servicing and no replacement is immediately available. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Begin the procedure because emergency airway equipment is needed only when a difficult airway has already been predicted
options.B: Proceed if routine oxygen and suction are available, then obtain advanced airway equipment only if ventilation becomes difficult
options.C: Do not begin deep sedation until appropriate emergency airway equipment is immediately available and confirmed functional
options.D: Proceed if the client has no history of difficult intubation because prior uncomplicated anesthesia excludes an unexpected airway emergency

rationale: Sedation and anesthesia can progress to airway compromise unexpectedly, so appropriate emergency airway and resuscitation equipment must be immediately available and functional before care begins. ASA guidance for sedation/anesthesia settings requires emergency airway equipment to be available and functional, and NCSBN identifies inspection and safe use of client-care equipment as an RN safety responsibility. A previously uncomplicated airway, absence of a predicted difficult airway, or availability of oxygen and suction alone does not eliminate the need for full emergency airway readiness.
educational_objective: Before deep sedation or anesthesia begins, the nurse verifies that required emergency airway equipment is immediately available and functional; a missing critical airway resource is a safety reason to delay the procedure until corrected.
source_document_title: Statement on Sedation & Anesthesia Administration in Dental Office-Based Settings
source_locator: Monitoring & Equipment; Resuscitative Measures & Protocols — appropriate monitors and safety equipment; emergency age-appropriate airway equipment immediately available and functional; equipment tested at accepted intervals
source_claim_supported: ASA states that settings providing sedation/anesthesia must have appropriate safety and resuscitative equipment, including emergency airway equipment, immediately available and functional, and that equipment must be checked/tested at accepted intervals.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment, printed p. 26 (PDF page 30): inspect equipment for safety hazards; facilitate appropriate and safe use of equipment
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — Safe Use of Equipment
correction_summary: Replaced difficult-airway-cart inventory trivia with a clinically actionable readiness decision for deep sedation. Avoided implying the RN selects airway devices or performs anesthesia management; final construct is verification of immediately available functional emergency equipment.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Official ASA statement verified; current ASA difficult-airway bibliography continues to cite the 2022 guideline. NCSBN 2026 safe-equipment language independently verifies the RN safety construct.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Immediate availability/functionality of emergency airway equipment is directly supported; no specific airway-device inventory is asserted.
audit_findings.choice_A: Incorrect; emergency airway readiness is required even without a predicted difficult airway.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; oxygen and suction alone do not replace immediately available emergency airway equipment.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; prior uncomplicated anesthesia does not guarantee absence of an unexpected airway emergency.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C meets the verified preprocedure safety requirement.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are realistic readiness decisions; inventory trivia and obvious device-name cues were removed.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct NCSBN 2026 Safe Use of Equipment mapping.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked scope, setting generalizability, predicted-airway assumptions, unsupported device lists, and second-answer risk; no unresolved conflict remains.
